subject: latent growth model with SRMR > 10 and even > 100

messages.author: 39f1ac78bd3926ba
messages.subject: latent growth model with SRMR > 10 and even > 100
parts:
Dear lavaan community,

I am running latent growth models on 10-wave data and now wanted to extend these models (which fit the data well) by including time-varying covariates that the observed data points used for the growth model are regressed on. These time-varying covariates are dichotomous items that indicate whether an even did or did not take place (1 or 0, respectively).

This works well for one of the events for which I include covariates, but not for the other. Specifically, when I include the covariates for the second event, my SRMR goes through the roof (> 900), even though the RMSEA and CFI both look fine. The SRMR becomes smaller the fewer time varying covariates I include for that second event, but only becomes acceptable if I exclude all covariates for this event.

Has anyone ever experienced a similar problem and if so, what did they then do to identify and potentially solve the problem?

Love to hear your suggestions!

Best wishes,
Elisabeth

messages.author: 39f1ac78bd3926ba
messages.subject: Re: latent growth model with SRMR > 10 and even > 100
parts:
In addition, it might be good that tinkering some more with the model, I also get the following warning:
lavaan WARNING: Hessian is not fully symmetric.

Moreover, another thing that's good to note is that we also had quite a lot of missings on part of the TVCs per event. So for instance they missed data on Wave 1-4, then had data at Wave 5-10. Sometimes these gaps could be filled logically by considering whether or not the event had already taken place, but other times not. In these cases, I used an 888 score so that R would not consider it missing and thus chuck out the entire case (because they would have data on other timepoints). I considered this would not be a problem because they also had missing data on the outcome/observed data point at that timepoint.

Best wishes,
Elisabeth

messages.subject: Re: latent growth model with SRMR > 10 and even > 100
parts: I used an 888 score so that R would not consider it missing and thus chuck out the entire case (because they would have data on other timepoints). I considered this would not be a problem because they also had missing data on the outcome/observed data point at that timepoint.

But the numerical value 888 is being interpreted as though that is part of the response scale for that variable.  So any misspecification involving that variable could appear orders of magnitude larger relative to setting a different missing code (e.g., -9).  If you are trying to use FIML, you can set missing = "fiml.x" to incorporate all available information on exogenous covariates, too.  

the SRMR becomes smaller the fewer time varying covariates I include for that second event, but only becomes acceptable if I exclude all covariates for this event.

Are you only estimating within-time regression slopes?  e.g., y1 ~ event1, y2 ~ event2, etc.
If so, then you are implicitly placing constraints that Time-t event has no direct impact on y at any other time points.  Despite it making sense, those constraints can create lots of large residuals, especially if there are other variables in your model besides the y variables.  The lavResiduals() output would show all the residuals in each model, which could be illuminating.
